review.summary: The executable rule exactly implements the R1 CPU budget obligation within the declared abstraction contract. It constrains every node, counts each assigned target Pod once, sums effective CPU requests, and permits equality with the remaining CPU budget. Effective request accounting, background reservations, units, and unknown observations are correctly delegated to the atom and semantic contracts.

obligation_checks.explanation: The clause "For each node" is represented by forall n:Node, with no additional guard or implication, matching the unguarded requirement. The body computes sum over the target Pod domain using ite(assign(p,n), cpu_request(p), 0), so exactly the targets selected for that node contribute once. It then applies le(sum, free_cpu(n)), which implements "must be <= free_cpu" and allows equality. Millicore units, effective request composition, background-request subtraction, and missing-observation behavior are supplied by the declared atom and semantic contracts rather than needing additional rule logic. The rendered rule matches the AST.

review.summary: The executable rule exactly implements the R2 node memory-budget requirement within the declared contracts and category scope. The rendered rule matches the AST.

obligation_checks.explanation: The requirement is unguarded “For each node.” The outer forall binds every Node without adding or omitting a guard. Its body compares sum over all target Pods of ite(assign(p,n), memory_request(p), 0) against free_memory(n) using le. Thus only targets assigned to the node consume its shared budget, equality passes, and unassigned targets contribute zero. Effective request calculation, byte units, background reservations, and missing-observation behavior are correctly delegated to the declared memory_request/free_memory and observation contracts.

The sum includes resource_request(p,r) exactly when assign(p,n) holds and compares that total with resource_free(n,r), preserving resource-name identity. The clause "Sum resource_request of assigned targets must be <= resource_free for that same resource name" is represented by Σp:Pod ite(assign(p,n), resource_request(p,r), 0) <= resource_free(n,r). Both request and free-budget calls use the same bound r, so vendor and partition resource names are not interchanged. The Pod domain contains only targets, while resource_free delegates background accounting to its atom contract. No extra availability, topology, health, or other-category constraint is added. The rendered formula faithfully matches the executable AST.

Its body sums ite(assign(p,n),1,0) over every target Pod p and compares the result to pod_slots(n) using le. This exactly enforces "Number of assigned target Pods must be <= pod_slots. Equality passes." No extra obligation is introduced, and both required atoms are used with correct sorts and arities.

review.summary: The two rules exactly encode the S1 obligations over all target Pods and referenced Claim identities. They neither add checks from S2/S3/S4 nor force any storage-path decision. The rendered rules match the supplied AST formulas.

review.summary: The three executable rules are well-formed and collectively match all declared S3 requirements within the scheduling-v2 semantic contract. Each obligation retains the required uses, claim_exists, and fixed_volume_exists guards, and no out-of-scope availability, configuration, topology, health, or uniqueness constraints are added.

Its implication consequence is exactly (dynamic(c) AND dynamic_eligible(c)) OR EXISTS v:Volume bind(c,v). Thus it checks the selected dynamic decision for eligibility or permits an existing static selection, without incorrectly disjoining the guard or requiring dynamic configuration.

For every such selected static binding, the consequent jointly requires class_ok, access_ok, mode_ok, capacity_ok, volume_available, and pv_selector_ok for the same c and v. Path existence remains correctly supplied by S3-R1 when the common guard holds, while uniqueness and static/dynamic exclusivity remain delegated to the shared axioms.
